_source_note: Template copy for the aplayermode.com Pinterest daily drip (owner-approved 16 Oct 2026). Every angle is written from what the named section of aplayermode/index.html itself says; nothing is invented and no price is typed (the only price on the page is the Founding 100 rate, and the drip carries none). Audience: planners, ADHD-routine and weekly-planning searchers. Anything that mentions ADHD says the app is a planning app, not medical advice. scripts/aplayermode/pin_queue.mjs turns these into dated variants ($0, no model call); tests/aplayermode/pinqueue.test.mjs checks the limits (title <= 100, description <= 500, no price, no Spry, no checkout).

founding-100.headline: Be one of the first 100 members.
founding-100.body: The Founding 100 get Executive Roundtable at a member rate that holds for as long as they stay subscribed.
founding-100.title: Founding 100: Join the First 100 Members of a Planning App That Plans Your Day
founding-100.description: A Player Mode is a planning app with a five-role executive team. The first 100 members get Executive Roundtable at a Founding rate that stays the same for as long as they stay subscribed. Your agenda is ready every morning, prioritised, and a missed day becomes a minimum day with no catch-up. Cancel any time.

founding-100.headline: Your agenda, ready every morning.
founding-100.body: Executive Roundtable turns a goal into a plan and the plan into daily steps, prioritised before you wake up.
points: Goal, then plan, then daily steps
One question at a time coaching
founding-100.title: Daily Planner App: Your Agenda Ready and Prioritised Every Morning
founding-100.description: Stop rebuilding your to-do list every morning. In A Player Mode's Executive Roundtable plan, your agenda is ready every morning and already prioritised: goal, then plan, then daily steps. It connects one calendar and one inbox, and coaches you one question at a time. Founding 100 places are open on the landing page.

founding-100.headline: It catches the promises you drop.
founding-100.body: Radar flags who you owe a reply, so nothing you said yes to slips through the week.
points: Flags who you owe a reply
founding-100.title: Planner App That Catches Dropped Promises and Flags Who You Owe a Reply
founding-100.description: Weekly planners hold tasks, not promises. A Player Mode's Radar catches the promises you dropped and flags who you owe a reply, alongside an agenda that is ready and prioritised every morning. It plans and coaches; you do the last step. See the plans and the Founding 100 on the A Player Mode page.

founding-100.headline: Missed yesterday? Get a minimum day.
founding-100.body: No catch-up list, no guilt. The plan shrinks to what still matters and you start again today.
founding-100.title: Missed a Day of Your Routine? A Planner That Gives You a Minimum Day, Not Catch-Up
founding-100.description: Most planners punish a missed day with a longer list. In A Player Mode, missing yesterday gets you a minimum day: no catch-up, no guilt, just what still matters today. It is part of every plan, including the Executive Roundtable plan the Founding 100 join. A planning app, not medical advice.

founding-100.headline: Who does the last step? You choose.
founding-100.body: Every plan does all five jobs. The only difference is who does the last step.
points: Autopilot: it does it, inside your rules
founding-100.title: Planning App With Three Plans: You Do It, You Tap Yes, or It Runs Inside Your Rules
founding-100.description: A Player Mode has three plans and each does all five executive jobs. The difference is who does the last step: in Executive Roundtable you do, in Executive Suite you tap yes and it does it, in Autopilot it handles recurring things on its own inside rules you set and you read the done-list. Founding 100 places are on the page.

founding-100.headline: Bills, birthdays, renewals: handled.
founding-100.body: Executive Suite tracks them and prepares each one for a one-tap approve.
points: Flags subscriptions you waste money on
founding-100.title: Life Admin Planner: Birthdays, Bills, Renewals and Appointments Ready to Approve
founding-100.description: Executive Suite in A Player Mode runs the life admin a paper planner only lists: birthdays, bills, renewals and appointments are tracked and prepared for a one-tap approve. It drafts the replies you owe, proposes the calendar fix and flags subscriptions you are wasting money on. It acts when you tap yes.

founding-100.headline: A five-person executive team in one app.
founding-100.body: It plans and coaches you; you do the last step. All five roles, every morning.
founding-100.title: A Five-Role Executive Team in One Planning App: Join the Founding 100
founding-100.description: Executive Roundtable puts five roles in one planning app: Executive Coach, Executive Assistant, Chief of Staff, Accountability Partner and Cognitive Behavioral Mindset Coach. Your agenda is ready every morning, prioritised, and coaching comes one question at a time. The first 100 members join as the Founding 100.

founding-100.headline: Recurring things, handled inside your rules.
founding-100.body: It saves money; it never spends it. A daily done-list shows what it did, with undo.
founding-100.title: Autopilot Planner: Follow-Ups, Flexible Meetings and Unused Subscriptions Handled
founding-100.description: A Player Mode's Autopilot plan handles recurring things on its own, inside standing rules you set: it sends follow-ups, moves flexible meetings, requests appointments by email and cancels unused subscriptions. It saves money and never spends it, and a daily done-list with undo shows what it did.

how-it-works.headline: A working plan in about 3 minutes.
how-it-works.body: Answer easy-tap questions. No essays. Stop any time; nothing is lost.
how-it-works.title: Weekly Planning in About 3 Minutes: Easy Taps, No Essays, a Working Plan
how-it-works.description: Setting up a planner should not take a weekend. A Player Mode asks easy-tap questions, about 3 minutes to a working plan, no essays, and nothing is lost if you stop. It builds your goals, your rules and your minimum day, and you approve each piece. Then every morning the plan is ready.

how-it-works.headline: Tap. Approve. Wake up to the plan.
how-it-works.body: Three steps, and you never design anything.
points: It builds your plan; you approve each piece
It runs your day, every morning
how-it-works.title: How to Plan Your Week Without Designing a Planner: Tap, Approve, Done
how-it-works.description: Three steps in A Player Mode: answer easy-tap questions (about 3 minutes), let it build your Mind, Body, Spirit plan and Tracks while you approve each piece, then wake up to the day already planned: one priority, a short start, then the day. You never design anything.

how-it-works.headline: One priority. A short start. Then the day.
how-it-works.body: Every morning your plan is ready. On Android it arrives at the time you set.
points: Then the rest of the day
Ready at the time you set
how-it-works.title: Simple Morning Routine Plan: One Priority, a Short Start, Then the Day
how-it-works.description: A Player Mode has your plan ready every morning in the same shape: one priority, a short start, then the day. On Android it arrives as a notification at the time you set; on the web it is waiting when you open the app. Bad days shrink automatically, with no catch-up and no guilt.

how-it-works.headline: Stop designing planners. Start the day.
how-it-works.body: You answer a few easy taps. It builds the plan and then carries the day.
how-it-works.title: Stop Overplanning: A Planner That Builds the Plan So You Just Start the Day
how-it-works.description: If you spend more time designing planners than using them, A Player Mode flips it: you answer a few easy taps and it builds the plan, then carries the day. Every morning: one priority, a short start, then the day. Bad days shrink automatically. You never design anything.

how-it-works.headline: Your goals, your rules, your minimum day.
how-it-works.body: It builds all three from your taps. You approve each piece before it runs.
how-it-works.title: Weekly Plan Builder: Goals, Rules and a Minimum Day You Approve Piece by Piece
how-it-works.description: A weekly plan that survives real life needs three things: goals, rules and a minimum day for when things go wrong. A Player Mode builds all three from a few easy taps, about 3 minutes, and you approve each piece before it runs. Then it has the day ready every morning.

how-it-works.headline: Bad days shrink automatically.
how-it-works.body: No catch-up, no guilt. The plan gets smaller instead of you falling behind.
how-it-works.title: A Weekly Planner for Real Life: Bad Days Shrink Automatically, No Catch-Up
how-it-works.description: Plans break when one bad day turns into a pile of catch-up. In A Player Mode, bad days shrink automatically: no catch-up, no guilt, and tomorrow's plan is still ready in the morning. Answer easy taps once, about 3 minutes, and it carries the days after that.

how-it-works.headline: Stop any time. Pick up where you left off.
how-it-works.body: Setup is easy taps, about 3 minutes, and nothing you answered is lost if you stop.
points: A working plan in about 3 minutes
how-it-works.title: Planner Setup You Can Stop Any Time: Easy Taps, Nothing Lost, About 3 Minutes
how-it-works.description: Long planner setups are where good intentions go to die. A Player Mode's setup is easy-tap questions, about 3 minutes to a working plan, and you can stop any time without losing anything. It builds your goals, rules and minimum day, and you approve each piece.

how-it-works.headline: Your plan arrives at the time you set.
how-it-works.body: On Android it is a notification at your time; on the web it is waiting when you open the app.
how-it-works.title: Daily Plan Notification at the Time You Set: One Priority, Then the Day
how-it-works.description: A Player Mode sends your daily plan to you instead of waiting for you to open a planner. On Android it arrives as a notification at the time you set; on the web it is waiting when you open the app. One priority, a short start, then the day.

app.headline: What do I do first this morning?
app.body: Max 5 physical steps, then the one task that matters.
app.title: ADHD-Friendly Morning Order: Feet to the Floor, Breathe, Water, Then One Task
app.description: When starting is the hard part, a ready order helps. A Player Mode has your morning order ready at the time you set: feet to the floor (10 seconds), 1 minute of breathing, a glass of water, then your highest-leverage step. Max 5 physical steps. A planning app, not medical advice or treatment.

app.kicker: Hard to get out of bed?
app.headline: A 10-minute routine you can do in bed.
app.body: You don't get advice. You get a ready in-bed mobility routine, Pilates-style, no equipment.
app.title: 10-Minute In-Bed Morning Routine for Days It Is Hard to Get Up (No Equipment)
app.description: "It's hard to get out of bed." A Player Mode does not answer with advice. It gives you a ready 10-minute in-bed mobility routine, Pilates-style with no equipment: belly breathing, pelvic tilts, knee hugs, a supine twist, dead bugs, glute bridges, a figure-4 stretch, then the edge of the bed and stand. A planning app, not medical advice.

app.headline: One step a day toward a big goal.
app.body: You pick the goal. It writes the 90-day plan and turns it into one step a day, at a safe pace.
app.title: Turn a Big Goal Into One Step a Day: A 90-Day Plan Written for You
app.description: Big goals stall on the first step. In A Player Mode you pick the goal, for example losing 20 lb, and it writes the 90-day plan and turns it into one step a day at a safe pace: walk 10 minutes today, put workout clothes out tonight, log what you eat, book a check-up. Never diet or medical advice.

app.headline: Starting is the hard part. So it's done for you.
app.body: Your morning order is ready at the time you set, so the first step is already decided.
points: Then the one task that matters
app.title: ADHD Routine Help When Starting Is the Hard Part: Your First Step Already Decided
app.description: If deciding what to do first eats your morning, A Player Mode decides it for you. Your morning order is ready at the time you set: max 5 physical steps, then the one task that matters. Bad days shrink automatically with no catch-up. A planning app, not medical advice or treatment.

app.kicker: The app that runs your day
app.headline: It runs your day. You just start.
app.body: You answer a few easy taps. It builds the plan and then carries the day.
points: Picks the moves and the order
app.title: The Planning App That Runs Your Day: Easy Taps Once, Then Just Start
app.description: A Player Mode is the app that runs your day for you. You answer a few easy taps, it builds the plan, then it carries the day: your morning order, the one task that matters, and a smaller day when things go wrong. You never design anything.

app.headline: You don't get advice. You get the plan.
app.body: Ask for help and it hands you the ready routine, with the moves and the order picked.
app.title: Less Decision Fatigue: A Planner That Hands You the Ready Routine, Not Tips
app.description: Advice is one more thing to decide about. When something is hard, A Player Mode hands you the ready routine with the moves and the order already picked, like a 10-minute in-bed mobility routine on a hard morning, or one safe step a day toward a 90-day goal. A planning app, not medical advice.

app.headline: Small daily steps. A safe pace.
app.body: It turns a health goal into one small step a day you can actually do.
app.title: Healthy Habit Planner: One Small Daily Step at a Safe Pace, Picked for You
app.description: Healthy habits stick when the daily step is small. A Player Mode turns a health goal into one step a day at a safe pace, such as a 10-minute walk, workout clothes out the night before, logging what you eat or booking a check-up. Never diet or medical advice.

app.headline: The whole day on one screen.
app.body: Open it and the day is there: one priority first, the rest in order.
points: A smaller day on bad days
app.title: Daily Planner App: The Whole Day on One Screen, One Priority First
app.description: A Player Mode puts the whole day on one screen when you open it: one priority first, a short start, then everything else in order. It is ready before you are, and on bad days the day is smaller instead of longer. Answer easy taps once to set it up.

modes.headline: One tap changes how it coaches you.
modes.body: You never have to say how you're feeling in a paragraph. Tap the mode; it adjusts the day and its voice.
modes.title: Five One-Tap Coaching Modes: Change the Day Without Explaining How You Feel
modes.description: In A Player Mode you never have to say how you are feeling in a paragraph. Tap a mode and it adjusts the day and its voice: High-Pressure when you are stuck, Executive Review when your head is full, Recovery after a bad day, Sprint near a deadline, Deep Work for one hard task.

modes.headline: Head full? Sort the 3 to 7 things.
modes.body: Executive Review adds no new ideas and no re-diagnosis. It organizes what you already know.
points: The 3 to 7 things you already know
modes.title: Brain Dump Too Big? Executive Review Organizes the 3 to 7 Things You Already Know
modes.description: When your head is full, more ideas make it worse. A Player Mode's Executive Review mode adds no new ideas and no re-diagnosis: it organizes the 3 to 7 things you already know into an order you can work. One tap, any time. A planning app, not medical advice.

modes.headline: Stuck? Get one stabilizing directive.
modes.body: High-Pressure mode cuts through the noise and ends with one thing to do now.
modes.title: Stuck or Procrastinating? High-Pressure Mode Ends With One Stabilizing Directive
modes.description: When you are stuck or avoiding something, a long list does not help. A Player Mode's High-Pressure coaching mode cuts through the noise and ends with one stabilizing directive: the one thing to do now. Tap it any time; you never have to explain how you feel.

modes.headline: A short, declared push on one thing.
modes.body: Sprint mode is for when a deadline is close: one thing only, for a declared stretch.
modes.title: Deadline Close? Sprint Mode Gives You a Short, Declared Push on One Thing Only
modes.description: Close to a deadline, the plan should get narrower, not longer. A Player Mode's Sprint mode is a short, declared push on one thing only, and everything else waits until it is done. One tap, any time, and the day and the coaching voice change with it.

modes.headline: Protect one block for one hard task.
modes.body: Deep Work mode protects one uninterrupted focus block for the task that matters.
points: The rest of the day around it
modes.title: Deep Work Planner: Protect One Uninterrupted Focus Block for One Hard Task
modes.description: A focus block only works if the rest of the day respects it. A Player Mode's Deep Work mode protects one uninterrupted focus block for one hard task and plans the rest of the day around it. Tap it on any time.

modes.headline: Low season? A minimum day, no guilt.
modes.body: Recovery mode is for after a bad day or a low season: a minimum day, no catch-up.
modes.title: Routine for Low-Energy Seasons: Recovery Mode Gives a Minimum Day, No Guilt
modes.description: Routines collapse in low seasons because they expect your best days. A Player Mode's Recovery mode gives you a minimum day after a bad day or in a low season: no catch-up, no guilt. One tap, no paragraph about how you feel. A planning app, not medical advice or treatment.

modes.headline: Tap how today is. The plan follows.
modes.body: Stuck, overloaded, low, rushed or focused: one tap and the day adjusts.
modes.title: ADHD-Friendly Planning: Tap How Today Is and the Plan Adjusts in One Tap
modes.description: Some days you are stuck, some days overloaded, some days low. In A Player Mode one tap matches the day: High-Pressure when stuck, Executive Review when your head is full, Recovery when low, Sprint near a deadline, Deep Work to focus. No paragraphs about feelings. A planning app, not medical advice.

modes.headline: No paragraphs about how you feel.
modes.body: Pick a mode with one tap. The day and the coaching voice change to match.
modes.title: A Planner That Adapts Without Journaling: One Tap Instead of a Paragraph
modes.description: Many planning apps want you to write about your mood before they help. A Player Mode skips it: tap one of five coaching modes and it adjusts the day and how it coaches you. High-Pressure, Executive Review, Recovery, Sprint or Deep Work, any time.

pillars.headline: Mind. Body. Spirit. Covered by default.
pillars.body: Every plan starts with all three, so the basics are covered without you deciding to cover them.
pillars.title: Mind, Body, Spirit Planner: All Three Covered by Default, No Deciding
pillars.description: A Player Mode starts every plan with Mind, Body and Spirit on, so the basics are covered without you deciding to cover them. Untick any you do not want it to hold for you; anything else you care about is sorted into one of the three automatically.

pillars.headline: The workout picked. Your sleep protected.
pillars.body: Movement, food, sleep and health routines, at a safe pace.
pillars.title: Fitness and Sleep Planner: The Workout Picked and Your Sleep Protected
pillars.description: Planning workouts and bedtimes by hand every week is a job. In A Player Mode the Body pillar picks the workout, protects your sleep and reminds you of the health routine, at a safe pace. It covers movement, food, sleep, weight and health routines. Never diet or medical advice.

pillars.headline: Room for faith, family and gratitude.
pillars.body: It makes room for them and repeats them on their own, without you guarding the time.
pillars.title: Planner With Time for Faith, Family and Gratitude Built In and Protected
pillars.description: The things that matter most are the first to fall off a busy week. A Player Mode's Spirit pillar makes room for faith, meditation, gratitude, nature, service, family and relationships, and repeats them on their own without you guarding the time.

pillars.headline: Keep the agenda on what moves the needle.
pillars.body: The Mind pillar picks the next thing to learn and keeps work to what matters.
pillars.title: Work Planner That Keeps Your Agenda on Work That Moves the Needle
pillars.description: Busy is not the same as moving forward. A Player Mode's Mind pillar keeps your agenda to work that moves the needle and picks the next thing to learn. It covers work, business and career, money, learning, focus and mental health. A planning app, not medical advice.

pillars.headline: Everything you care about, in three places.
pillars.body: Anything else you care about is sorted into Mind, Body or Spirit automatically.
points: One plan for all of it
pillars.title: Whole-Life Planner: Everything You Care About Sorted Into Mind, Body or Spirit
pillars.description: Life planners fall apart when every goal needs its own page. A Player Mode sorts anything you care about into Mind, Body or Spirit automatically, so one plan holds all of it. All three are on by default; untick any you do not want it to hold for you.

pillars.headline: A balanced week without the spreadsheet.
pillars.body: Work, workouts, sleep, faith and family all get a place in the plan.
pillars.title: Balanced Weekly Plan Without the Spreadsheet: Work, Body and Family Covered
pillars.description: Balancing work, workouts, sleep, faith and family by hand every week is exhausting. A Player Mode covers Mind, Body and Spirit by default: it keeps work to what moves the needle, picks the workout, protects your sleep and makes room for family and faith.

pillars.headline: Self-care that repeats on its own.
pillars.body: Gratitude, nature, meditation and family time come back each week without you guarding it.
pillars.title: Self-Care Planner That Repeats On Its Own: Gratitude, Nature and Family Time
pillars.description: Self-care slips when it depends on remembering. In A Player Mode the Spirit pillar makes room for gratitude, nature, meditation, service and family time, and repeats them on their own without you guarding the time. On by default in every plan.

pillars.headline: Health routines, reminded at a safe pace.
pillars.body: Movement, food, sleep and weight goals become small reminders you can keep.
pillars.title: Health Routine Planner: Movement, Food and Sleep Reminders at a Safe Pace
pillars.description: A Player Mode's Body pillar turns movement, food, sleep and weight goals into small reminders and a picked workout, at a safe pace, so health routines do not depend on willpower. Never diet or medical advice; a planning app.
